title: The Responsive Eye
lede: William C. Seitz’s catalogue for the Museum of Modern Art’s 1965 exhibition of optical art, with Bridget Riley’s Current printed edge to edge on the cover.
summary: A cover filled with fine black and white wave stripes, overprinted with the title in several colours. MoMA, 1965.

source.label: UbuWeb: scan of The Responsive Eye (MoMA, 1965)

creator.name: William C. Seitz (author); Joseph Bourke Del Valle (designer); The Museum of Modern Art

evidence.note: Downloaded the UbuWeb PDF scan and inspected the cover and the first pages as extracted page images (2538 × 2793 px) in a scratchpad. The faint colophon reads as the third printing, 1966. MoMA’s own exhibition page returned HTTP 403. No image is stored.

styles.note: The exhibition catalogue that fixed op art in public view, with a black and white Riley wave field as its cover.

context: The title page reads “The Responsive Eye, by William C. Seitz, The Museum of Modern Art, New York”, in collaboration with the City Art Museum of St. Louis, the Contemporary Art Council of the Seattle Art Museum, the Pasadena Art Museum, and the Baltimore Museum of Art. [UbuWeb scan](https://ubu.com/historical/responsive/ResponsiveEyeMOMA1965.pdf).

Seitz’s acknowledgments say that the exhibition was announced in November 1962, and that “the catalogue was designed by Joseph Bourke Del Valle of the Museum’s Department of Publications”. [UbuWeb scan](https://ubu.com/historical/responsive/ResponsiveEyeMOMA1965.pdf).

David Zwirner says that Seitz included Riley’s *Current* (1964) and *Hesitate* (1964), and that “the eye-popping black-and-white squiggles of Riley’s Current adorned the catalogue cover”. [David Zwirner](https://www.davidzwirner.com/news/2019/bridget-riley-s-paintings-continue-to-mesmerize-six-decades-on).
observed: The whole cover is filled with thin vertical black and white stripes that wave; the waves tighten toward the left and right edges and toward the middle.
“THE RESPONSIVE EYE” is set four times in condensed sans-serif capitals, overprinted in yellow, magenta, green, and red, slightly offset from one another across the middle.
The coloured letters take on the stripes of the ground, so the title seems to vibrate and blur.
The title page inside is plain: “The Responsive Eye” in a black condensed grotesque, with the author and publisher in small serif capitals on white.
interpretation: The cover shows the style’s rule for type on pattern in its display form: large letters may carry the stripes, while the inside pages keep text on plain white.
The offset colour overprints are a graphic-design addition to Riley’s black and white field, and they go beyond the style’s one-accent rule.
borrow: Fill a cover or hero panel with one black and white wave field, edge to edge.
Let display letters show the pattern through them, and move all reading text to a plain page.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The catalogue is © The Museum of Modern Art, 1965, and the cover reproduces a work by a living artist.
